question: For the canonical q=1 square and a straight separator, do the two logical sectors induce overlapping laws of the complete interface flux U?

setting.geometry: canonical L by L square with unmeasured left and right rough boundaries
setting.edge_partition: A contains exactly the edges whose two endpoints have x<=k; B contains all other edges
setting.interface_state: U_v=(D_A j)_v for v in S
setting.public_record: Q=(D_M j) on every measured vertex
setting.logical_bit: absolute activity parity on the right rough-boundary cut; a Q-dependent reference relabeling changes only the known additive constant

exact_identity.formula: H = [sum_{v in M, x(v)>=k} Q_v + sum_{v in S} U_v] mod 2
exact_identity.proof: Sum the B-edge divergence over all measured B vertices S union {k<x<L-1}. Every B edge between measured vertices cancels modulo two. The only uncancelled B edges are the right rough-boundary cut edges. On S, D_B j=Q-U; minus and plus coincide modulo two.
exact_identity.scope: finite-graph topology; no probability, mixing, asymptotic or path-counting assumption

consequences.sector_support: For every public Q with both sectors supported, pi_0^Q and pi_1^Q occupy disjoint parity classes of U.
consequences.conditional_information: I(H;U|Q)=H(H|Q), so the prior information bound is also an identity-level envelope rather than a contraction theorem.

scientific_decision.reason: The complete flux variable contains the logical bit as a deterministic parity. No model-specific estimate can make d_Q<1 on ambiguous records.
scientific_decision.next_target: If gluing is retained, first quotient or align the deterministic topological parity and compare the residual interface laws under an explicit sector-switching transport; otherwise return directly to a physical lower-tail or contour bound for the global sector ratio.

claim_boundary: This closes the proposed contraction route for the complete straight-separator flux U. It does not prove or disprove square correctability, construct a useful parity-aligned coupling, or locate a transition.
